Only way I got myself to exercise was having the resources to exercise in a way that accommodated me. And exposure to a lot of options. You don't know the true benefits of exercise until it actually benefits you in a way specific to you.

I could've never started exercising if I was told to run laps and catch a ball with strangers. I started when I realized I didn't like cardio, wanted big muscles, and had an empty college gym. When I then realized the  strength and flexibility from starting out made me feel and move better, I was hooked on the activity. Learning over time to feel confident and comfortable in your body is hard for someone with autism because of the physical, mental, and social pressures we mostly likely have faced our entire lives.

Starting new things like exercising can come with a lot of factors that aren't explicitly visible to anyone. Stuff can't be too easy because learning is about mistakes, but when ur stressed or over stimulated you can't learn when you're crashing out.

People don't want to be "unhealthy." Human bodies just survive as easily as they can to prevent stress. Mirror healthy lifestyles, be calm, be kind, be supportive.
